windows.model_format: DeviceModelPretty of real DMI records: SystemProductName, else SystemFamily + BaseBoardProduct; 15 chars, HP names up to 32
sources: https://github.com/linuxhw/DMI -- real dmidecode output collected from Linux machines
https://endoflife.date/api/windows.json -- release and support dates behind the version weights (read by hand, not fetched)
notes: Version weights approximate the installed base after Windows 10 went end of support on 2025-10-14.
Hardware era is not matched against the Windows version; the pool is limited to current hardware instead.
No arm64 version is listed. SystemVersionPretty writes arm64 only on an ARM machine and every model in this pool is x86, so the string would have to be paired with hardware that cannot run it.

Model strings are produced by running lib_base's own DeviceModelPretty over real dmidecode records, so a machine whose product name the client would reject appears as its family + board or not at all. This is why most Lenovo entries are machine type codes and HP entries keep their 'HP ' prefix: that is what the firmware reports.

linux.model_format: DeviceModelPretty of real DMI records: product_name, else product_family + board_name; 15 chars, HP names up to 32
linux.version_format: uname sysname (plus the release off Linux) + XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP parts + session type + libc
sources: https://github.com/linuxhw/DMI -- real dmidecode output collected from Linux machines
https://repology.org/api/v1/project/glibc -- glibc versions behind the LIBC table (read by hand, not fetched)
notes: Version strings are every combination of kernel, desktop environment, session type and libc.
Weights are popularity estimates, not measurements; desktop and session shares follow common distro defaults.

A non-glibc system carries no libc part at all, because GetLibcVersion returns nothing outside glibc and the whole clause is then skipped. FreeBSD additionally carries uname's release, which lib_base appends everywhere except Linux.

The model pool adds what Windows has no equivalent for: systemd-detect-virt names (uppercased, for virtual machines) and SMBIOS chassis types, which base_info_linux.cpp falls back to when DMI exposes no usable product name.
